activities.title: Light arrives as a stream of photons
Below the threshold frequency, nothing happens
Brighter light: more photons, more electrons
Misconception: brighter light ejects faster electrons

assessmentPoints: Photon answers in the stream of photons activity
Trap answers in the misconception activity
objectives.text: Describe light as a stream of photons, each carrying energy E = h f

assessmentPoints: Threshold and work function answers in the threshold activity
Equation and stopping potential answers in the equation and brighter light activities
successCriteria: The work function W is the minimum energy an electron needs to escape the metal surface. The threshold frequency f0 = W / h is the lowest frequency whose photons each carry at least W; below f0 no electrons are emitted, however bright the light.
objectives.text: Use h f = W + KE_max, the threshold frequency f0 = W / h and the stopping potential e V_s = KE_max

assessmentPoints: Brighter light answers in the brighter light activity
Trap answers in the misconception activity
successCriteria: λ = h / (m v) = 6.63 x 10^-34 / (9.11 x 10^-31 x 1.0 x 10^6) = 7.3 x 10^-10 m. A moving electron carries a wavelength just like a photon: matter shows wave-particle duality.
Brightness means more photons, not stronger ones: a dim violet beam ejects faster electrons than a bright red one.
objectives.text: Explain wave-particle duality with de Broglie's λ = h / (m v), and avoid the brighter-means-faster trap
